Joby Aviation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio based defense technology company, for roughly $500 million. The deal marks a major step forward for Joby's defense business, adding scale through a profitable, fast growing company already supporting active U.S. national security programs. Founded in 2015, Resonant employs about 250 people, more than 90% of whom hold security clearances. Resonant's growth has been substantial. Trailing 12-month revenue topped $100 million, up roughly 40% year over year, while the company has maintained high-teens adjusted EBITDA margins that are expected to climb further as production ramps up. Demand has only accelerated. In the first half of 2026, bookings came in at more than three times the volume seen in the same period of 2025, and backlog more than doubled year over year. hits.title: Joby to buy Resonant Sciences, establish defense business in $500 million deal - Breaking Defense
hits.snippet: WASHINGTON — Electric aircraft startup [Joby Aviation](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/joby/) has agreed to acquire the military technology firm Resonant Sciences and convert the Dayton, Ohio-based company into Joby’s dedicated defense business, the two companies announced today. The $500 million acquisition consists of roughly $450 million in cash and $50 million in Joby common stock, according to a joint [press release](https://www.jobyaviation.com/news/joby-aviation-to-scale-defense-business-through-acquisition-of-resonant-sciences) from both companies. The transaction is expected to close “in the first half of 2027,” subject to regulatory approval. Joby is one of several electric air taxi services racing to market targeting point-to-point shuttling in urban environments — an ambition broadly slowed by developmental challenges and regulatory hurdles.
